newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Peregrine plans Samurai bond for June.
newsitem.headline: Peregrine plans Samurai bond for June.

text.p: Peregrine Investments Holdings Ltd said it would launch its three-year 30 billion yen Samurai bond in June, taking advantage of Japan's low interest rates and broad savings base.

Roadshows would begin on June 9 in Japan and the issue was expected to close by the end of June, John Lee, Peregrine's managing director, treasury and risk management with the executive committee, told a news conference.
"It is the right time to go to Japan now, " Lee said. " Japan has a strong asset and large saving base."
He said Japanese investors were looking for good quality Asian credit.
He said he expected the Samurai to receive a BBB-plus rating from Japan Bond Research Institute, equivalent to Peregrine's rating for unsecured long-term debt.
The facility had two tranches, one fixed-rate and the other a floating-rate, targeting different investor bases, Lee said.
Both tranches would have a three-year tenor, and Nikko Securities was the arranger, he said.
Pricing would be set in two or three weeks, Lee said.
Lee said Japanese investors would probably find the indicative pricing attractive given Peregrine's rarity value in the Samurai market and its expected JBRI rating, he said.
Lee said it was "very likely" Peregrine would swap issue proceeds into U.S. dollars, to hedge against yen volatility.
Peregrine had not applied for ratings from Moody's Investors Services and Standard & Poor's, but might do so in 1998, he said.
"It is certain that Peregrine can receive an above investment-grade rating", Lee said while declining to specify what rating he expected.
